label: TP
reason: Both alerts are True Positives. The switch statement in doSomething (line 72) sets switchTarget to 'B' (from "ABC"), which triggers the safe branch (bar="bob"). However, the XSS alert targets the catch block (line 61-62) where the exception handler prints the raw SQL containing 'bar'. Since EmptyResultDataAccessException is thrown when no rows match, and attackers can craft payloads to cause this (e.g., by making the password comparison fail), the raw user input reaches the HTML sink. The SQL injection alert correctly flags the dependency on user input in the query string. Both represent real vulnerabilities.

evidence.note: XSS sink in catch block reflects raw bar (potentially user input) to HTML
SQL injection sink depends on bar which may contain user input
